exposure: fetal-maternal HLA mismatches (low vs. high allogeneic pregnancies)
preeclamptic OD pregnancies vs. healthy OD pregnancies
outcome: effector/memory Tregs expressing PD-1 and Helios
cohort: The study included ten healthy and five preeclamptic oocyte donation (OD) pregnancies.
finding: Early high allogeneic OD pregnancies showed a reduction in Tregs and CD8+ T cells, along with increased IL-6 and progesterone, while preeclamptic OD pregnancies exhibited reduced CD45RO+CTLA-4+ Tregs and increased TGF-b1/-b2 levels in early stages, and higher CD45RO+TIGIT+ Tregs and TNFa in late stages, compared to healthy OD pregnancies.
